query: Consider the following context: The recent trend of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) was studied extensively for their promising mechanical properties, but individual constituents' effects have remained unexplored. In that context, which method can be used for the effects of changing the percentage of elements of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA on the mechanical properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A supervised machine learning (ML) framework, combined with a systematic design-of-experiments approach to vary each element’s fraction in HfNbTaTiZr-based high-entropy alloys (HEAs), will isolate and quantify individual constituent effects on mechanical properties, enabling prediction and optimization of mechanical performance.
generation.material_initial_state: Initially equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr-HEA produced via a standard powder-metallurgy or arc-melting route, fully consolidated and homogenized.
generation.intervention: Systematically modify the at.% of each element (Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, Zr) in small increments using a statistically designed array of compositions and fabricate and test each variant.
generation.conditions: Perform high-throughput mechanical characterization (hardness, tensile strength, ductility) under ambient conditions, controlling for sample preparation and oxygen content to reduce confounding effects.
generation.structural_mediator: Elemental variations alter microstructure (e.g., phase distributions, lattice distortion, grain size) and thus affect yield strength and ductility.
generation.mechanism: ML-based regression or neural networks reveal how each atomic percent shift impacts solid-solution strengthening, lattice distortion, and possibly phase stability, leading to correlations with mechanical performance.
generation.predicted_outcome: We expect distinct trends linking individual element content to changes in strength and ductility; for example, incremental increases in certain elements may promote solid-solution strengthening with moderate or moderate-to-strong improvements in hardness and yield strength.
generation.baseline: Mechanical properties of the near-equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr-HEA serve as the reference.
generation.boundary: Extreme deviations from near-equiatomic compositions might introduce additional phases and complexities that fall outside straightforward ML-based predictive accuracy.
generation.uncertainty: The role of each element (especially Hf, Nb, and Ta) in modifying mechanical properties is not fully resolved, so precise quantitative effects remain uncertain until verified by experimentation.

falsification_experiment.design: Use a factorial design approach to synthesize multiple HfNbTaTiZr compositions with controlled incremental changes in each element's atomic percentage (e.g., from 5% to 35% in 5% steps), produce samples via the same processing route, measure mechanical properties, and compare the results to ML predictions.
measurements: Tensile properties (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, elongation)
Microstructure examination (e.g., XRD, SEM/EDS) to quantify phase stability and measure grain size
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured mechanical properties do not correlate with or systematically deviate from the ML model’s predictions across the studied composition range, the hypothesis that a supervised ML approach can accurately and robustly quantify individual elemental effects on mechanical properties is not supported.

cited_evidence.text: High entropy alloys (HEAs), complex concentrated alloys (CCAs), and multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) are the most common names of a new group of materials [ [1] , [2] , [3] , [4] , [5] ] introduced by Yeh et al. [ [6] ] and Cantor et al. [ [7] ] in the beginning of this century. Many definitions were proposed for such materials, but in general they consist of multiple (usually at least five) elements in equiatomic or near-equiatomic composition [ [2] ]. This approach is different from the traditional alloy design using one (or maximum two) principal element and other minor elements. The presence of many elements in equiatomic (or near) composition leads to high mixing entropy and thus to many interesting properties [ [2] , [5] ]. One of such effects is the existence of a random solid solution and simple body centered cubic (bcc) or faced centered cubic (fcc) structure. Recently HEAs with hexagonal closed packed (hcp) structure have been reported as well [ [8] , [9] ]. A new approach to HEA design using the valence electron concentration (VEC) was recently proposed with the aim of increasing the plasticity of these alloys [ [10] , [11] ]. The concept of HEAs provides us an unprecedented degree of freedom in the design of advanced alloys with promising properties. For the rapid exploration of the vast compositional space and investigation of the composition and temperature effects on the microstructure, advanced HEA-design strategies and efficient tools are necessary. At present, a few advanced HEA-design strategies were reported by combining the physicochemical criteria, CALPHAD, data mining, and multi-objective optimization algorithm [21] , [22] , [35] – [37] , demonstrating that the CALPHAD method has played an important role in the design of advanced HEAs. There are two essential requirements to carry out calculations, using the CALPHAD method: computational software and database.

decision.trend: In the cited work on HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy, researchers focused on processing via routes such as cold isostatic pressing, sintering, HIP, swaging, and spark plasma sintering followed by high-pressure torsion. These approaches successfully improved density and hardness while controlling oxygen pickup and refining grains. However, all efforts primarily examined an equiatomic composition, and the specific influence of varying each element’s percentage within the same five-element system was not systematically explored.
decision.unsolved: A direct, systematic method to correlate mechanical properties with incremental changes in each constituent’s concentration for HfNbTaTiZr remains missing. Identifying the individual roles of Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr in mechanical response and designing predictable property–composition relationships has not yet been fully achieved.
decision.lever: Establish a supervised ML framework that couples a design-of-experiments approach (varying each element’s fraction systematically), high-throughput mechanical testing, and multi-parameter regression or neural networks
decision.why: This approach enables efficient exploration of the five-dimensional compositional space while directly correlating changes in each element’s content to mechanical performance. The resulting predictive models can then guide the identification of optimal compositions for enhanced strength and ductility, addressing the open question of individual elemental contributions in HfNbTaTiZr-HEAs.
